title: KV calibration ensemble profiles and LLM consistency suite
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define and evaluate an 'ensemble' approach to KV cache quantization profiles (INT8 + FP8 mixes) plus a reproducible consistency test suite for accuracy regressions across formats and sequence-length distributions. Goal: find profile combinations that reduce per-token cost without >1.0% downstream metric regressions while staying within p99 latency SLO budget.
background: Existing experiments focused on single-profile calibrations (int8-only or fp8-only) per-model. We see workload heterogeneity: short chat interactions and long-context retrievals exhibit different KV magnitude distributions. A single static profile under-optimizes either cost or quality. The team proposed combining multiple calibrated profiles and routing requests by sequence-length and head-wise variance to get better trade-offs. We need a reproducible harness and acceptance criteria to approve rollouts.
proposed_solution: 1) Build an ensemble profile scheduler that selects among pre-calibrated INT8/FP8 profiles based on runtime heuristics (prefix length, request type, per-request variance estimate). 2) Implement light per-head bias-correction in the runtime to compensate for systematic drift after quantization. 3) Construct an LLM consistency suite containing domain-diverse prompts, adversarial token sequences, and production-sampled traces for regression monitoring. 4) Run controlled chaos tests that inject sequence-length distribution shifts to validate fallback behavior.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline calibration - generate candidate profiles for short (<64 tokens), mid (64-512), and long (>512) sequences using holdout calibration sets; include per-layer/per-head scale factors.
Phase B: Ensemble scheduler - implement low-overhead routing heuristic in runtime and shadow-serve 10% of traffic to ensemble profiles (no rollout) for metric collection.
Phase C: Bias-correction - add per-head additive bias term learned from calibration set and validate improvement on QA/LM perplexity.
Phase D: Consistency suite - run the suite nightly with p95/p99 latency and quality deltas logged; include adversarial and production-sampled slices.
Phase E: Canary rollout - 1% traffic for 48 hours, 10% for 72 hours with automated rollback on threshold triggers.
Phase F: Postmortem & operationalization - document scheduling knobs, cost impact, and recommendations for default settings per model class.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end downstream metric regression (EM for QA, token-level perplexity) <= 1.0% relative to FP32 baseline on the consistency suite
Embedding cosine drift <= 0.005 on retrieval test set
p99 latency increase <= 8ms (absolute) and <= 5% relative against current baseline for the same throughput
No more than two user-visible regression alerts in a 30-day synthetic run
Automated rollback triggers and healthchecks validated in canary runs
metrics: cost_per_1M_tokens: measure after batching and caching savings
throughput_rps: tokens/sec normalized to dedicated capacity profile
rollout_plan: Shadow (10%): collect metrics without impacting live responses
Canary (1%): short low-risk live traffic with auto-rollback thresholds
Expanded Canary (10% for 72h): validate under more load and diurnal patterns
Gradual ramp to target (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with pause windows and weekly checkpoints
Ops runbook: rollback command, telemetry dashboards, and incident channels listed
dependencies: benchmarks: updated perf harness for long-context traces
